title: VPC Operator Handoff: Automation Recipes and Safety Checklist
author: Priya Menon
summary: A practical, automation-first checklist and set of recipes to hand off VPC-based private deployments from Field Delivery to Operator teams. Emphasizes safe cutovers, automated validations, smoke tests, and rollback triggers tailored for heterogeneous customer networks.
body:
Purpose and scope:

This document standardizes the handoff process for Redwood Private VPC deployments where the delivery/implementation team transfers operational responsibility to the customer operator or Redwood operator team. It focuses on small-to-medium enterprise VPC installs (single-region, multi-AZ) with optional peering/interconnect to customer networks.

Audience:
- Field Delivery engineers (install & integration)
- Customer Operators / SREs
- Redwood Operator oncall and support engineers

Risk assumptions and constraints:
- Operators may have limited privileged access during initial handoff (least-privilege model).
- Network paths to telemetry backplane may be intermittent; recipes include offline-acceptance steps.
- Some customers enforce strict egress and KMS policies; automation must support allowlisted endpoints and pre-approved cert bundles.

High-level 3-phase handoff model:
1) Install & integration (Field Delivery) — deliver working topology and evidence artifacts.
2) Operator acceptance (Operator Team) — run automated validations and live traffic smoke tests.
3) Transfer of responsibility (Formal cutover) — finalize SLAs, incident routing, credentials, and rollback windows.

Ownership and roles:
- Field Delivery: installs components, provides artifact bundle, initial walk-through.
- Customer Operator: runs acceptance suite, confirms SLA targets locally.
- Redwood Operator (optional): co-validates telemetry, config drift checks, and stays on-call for the first 72 hours.

Acceptance criteria (must all pass before cutover):
- Health checks: all services report READY and < 1% error-rate on synthetic requests for 10 minutes.
- Latency SLOs: 95p token generation latency within agreed threshold (default 300ms for short seqs) on internal synthetic load.
- Telemetry: logs, metrics, and traces reach the configured aggregation endpoint; sampling rate >= configured baseline.
- Security: KMS integration verified, certificate chain validated, and RBAC for operator roles tested.
- Backups: model artifact snapshot and runtime KV snapshot created and stored in approved artifact store.

Operator acceptance checklist (step-by-step):
1. Pre-checks (run as Field Delivery with operator present):
   - Confirm network ACLs, VPC route tables, and peering entries match the delivered pairing document.
   - Verify DNS resolution for control plane endpoints from operator network.
   - Export and hand over these artifacts: topology diagram (PNG), CIDR mapping CSV, operator-keys.md (redacted), and the delivery manifest JSON.

2. Automated validation suite (operator runs):
   - Execute the provided acceptance script: ./acceptance/run_all.sh --env vpc --retry 3
   - Script steps (examples):
     a) net-check: verifies egress connectivity to telemetry and license endpoints using tcping and TLS verify.
     b) health-check: queries /internal/health endpoints across control plane and runtime nodes.
     c) perf-smoke: runs a 5-minute synthetic generation at 10 concurrent users and records p50/p95 latencies.
     d) kv-consistency: write/read KV test to confirm ephemeral store correctness.

   - Expected output: a single acceptance artifact: acceptance-report-<customer>-YYYYMMDD.json containing pass/fail and timestamps.

3. Live traffic smoke (operator with Field Delivery observation):
   - Canary traffic profile (3 buckets):
     1) Tokenized short prompts (10 RPS) – latency/SLO validation
     2) Medium prompts with KV reuse (2 RPS) – KV cache correctness
     3) Embedding batch test (1 RPS) – throughput and memory pressure check

   - Observe: no error spikes > 2% across any route, no OOM events, and healthy GPU utilization < 85% sustained.

4. Security handoff:
   - Rotate temporary keys to operator-managed keys using the key-rotation CLI: redwood-keys rotate --target customer-kms --validate
   - Verify audit logging: sample 100 auth events and confirm UIDs and source IPs match expected operator ranges.

Automation recipes and examples:

A) Acceptance orchestration (example: Kubernetes Job manifests and local wrapper)
- Purpose: run acceptance steps in-cluster (recommended for customers who restrict operator outbound).
- Example job wrapper (YAML as string):
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: acceptance-batch-run
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: acceptance
        image: redwood/acceptance:2026-03
        args: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "./run_all.sh --env vpc --output /artifacts/report.json"]
      restartPolicy: Never
      serviceAccountName: acceptance-runner

Notes: mount the /artifacts volume to an S3/GCS-compatible bucket or to an NFS share that the operator can fetch. Ensure serviceAccount has minimum IAM scope.

B) Lightweight operator CLI recipes
- net-check snippet (bash):
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
ENDPOINTS=("telemetry.redwood.internal:443" "license.redwood.internal:443")
for e in "${ENDPOINTS[@]}"; do
  timeout 5 bash -c "cat < /dev/null > /dev/tcp/$(echo $e | cut -d: -f1)/$(echo $e | cut -d: -f2)" || { echo \"FAILED $e\"; exit 2; }
done
echo \"NET-OK\"

C) Automated rollback trigger (operator policy)
- Purpose: if acceptance or early cutover detects sustained errors, trigger coordinated rollback with artifact snapshot restore.
- Simple policy: if error-rate > 5% for 10 minutes or p95 latency > 2x threshold for 5 minutes, initiate rollback.
- Command to start rollback: redwood-operator rollback --source snapshot://artifacts/<customer>/pre-cutover-YYYYMMDD --target runtime-stack --preserve-logs

Cutover orchestration and timing guidance:
- Prefer a 48-hour rolling window for non-critical customers, 72-hour observation for enterprise customers with Redwood Operator on-call.
- Cutover steps (numbered):
  1. Freeze non-essential config pushes and scheduled jobs.
  2. Ensure at least two independent artifact snapshots exist and checksums verified.
  3. Run acceptance suite and store report in customer artifact bucket.
  4. Rotate keys to operator-managed KMS.
  5. Transition monitoring/alerting contacts to Operator paging policy.
  6. Announce cutover start and expected rollback window to stakeholders.
  7. Switch traffic via the agreed routing policy and monitor for at least 30 minutes; extend to 2 hours for noisy tenants.

Rollback procedure (detailed):
- Preconditions: latest working snapshot exists and was verified during acceptance.
- Steps:
  1. Set runtime to safemode: redwood-runtime safemode --drain=false --route-fallback local
  2. Trigger snapshot restore: redwood-operator restore --snapshot-id pre-cutover-YYYYMMDD --force
  3. Validate KV and model artifacts using the smoke validator: ./tools/smoke-validate --post-restore
  4. If validation passes, flip traffic back and document incident. If validation fails, escalate to Escalation Playbook (see related_pages).

Monitoring and alert thresholds (recommended defaults):
- Service health: alert at 5m if any service reports status != READY.
- Error-rate: page at 2% sustained for 5 minutes; critical at 5% sustained for 2 minutes.
- Latency: page if p95 > 2x baseline for 10 minutes.
- Telemetry backlog: page if telemetry queue depth > 30 minutes of lag.

Evidence artifacts to hand over (minimum set):
- delivery-manifest.json (topology + node inventory + image checksums)
- acceptance-report-<customer>-YYYYMMDD.json
- model-snapshot-<id>.sha256
- kv-snapshot-<id>.sha256
- access-rotation-plan.md (who, when, how keys rotate)
- runbooks: operator-quickstart.md and incident-template.md

Operator runbook summary (quick commands):
- check cluster health: redwood-cli cluster status --format short
- view recent errors: redwood-cli logs query --since 15m --level error
- trigger acceptance: ./acceptance/run_all.sh --env vpc
- initiate rollback: redwood-operator rollback --source snapshot://...

Special cases and divergence recipes:
- Air-gapped sites: use offline acceptance runner with signed artifacts and an offline telemetry ingestion stub. See the onprem-packaging docs for attestation steps.
- Strict KMS customers: pre-stage encrypted model bundles and supply KMS key policy templates in the artifact bundle.
- Heterogeneous GPU fleets: include per-node micro-benchmarks in delivery-manifest and use node-label-driven traffic steering during smoke.

Appendix A — Example acceptance report schema (flattened):
- id: string
- customer: string
- run_start: timestamp
- run_end: timestamp
- checks: list_of_strings (net-check, health-check, perf-smoke, kv-consistency)
- results_summary: string (PASS | WARN | FAIL)
- artifacts: list_of_strings (paths)
- operator_signoff: name,email,timestamp

Appendix B — Troubleshooting notes (common failures):
- Telemetry failing to reach endpoint: check outbound rules, TLS inspection devices, and verify CA bundle.
- High p95 on short prompts: check KV hit-rate and whether batching is erroneously enabled for low-latency routes.
- OOM during embedding batch: reduce batch size and confirm quantization profile applied.

Related documents and references:
- See the private deploy oncall runbook for escalation numbers and templates.
- Refer to the packaging attestation doc for air-gapped acceptance variants.
